gold.verbatim: established in 2009 by the Marine Research Council
340 kilometres of the eastern seaboard
2023 operating budget of £8.7 million
directed by Dr. Amara Okonjo, who succeeded Dr. Peter Lindqvist in April 2022
The programme maintains 74 permanent monitoring stations
Net shoreline retreat across the monitored coast averaged 1.8 metres in 2023
compared with 1.1 metres in 2022 and a ten-year mean of 0.9 metres
Storm Bettina produced a peak significant wave height of 9.4 metres at the Ravensmouth buoy on 12 November 2023
Storm Cyrus followed on 23 November, generating a storm surge of 2.3 metres above predicted tide level at Sandhaven
Twelve of the 74 stations recorded net accretion rather than erosion
1.24 million cubic metres of sand left the monitored cell in 2023
approximately 62% was transported offshore beyond the closure depth
sediment retention behind the Kelbrook Reservoir, completed in 2019
Dune vegetation cover was surveyed at 22 sites
Mean cover fell from 71% in 2022 to 64% in 2023
A trial planting of 40,000 marram culms was carried out at Thornwick Bay in March 2023
Three monitoring stations were lost during Storm Bettina: stations 31, 44 and 52
Replacement cost is estimated at £46,000 per station
Data completeness for the year was 94.1%, down from 97.6% in 2022
The programme adopted a new grain-size analysis protocol in January 2023
submitted evidence to the parliamentary Coastal Resilience Inquiry in May 2023
The programme intends to install eight additional stations in 2024
Dr. Okonjo will step down as director in September 2024
